title: Migrate Go logging from log package to slog
description: Brownfield Go migration: replace stdlib log calls in a service module with slog structured logging. The function signatures and behavior must remain identical; only the logging calls change.

task_spec.prompt:
Migrate service.go from log to slog.

Replace:
  import "log"
  log.Printf(...)

With:
  import "log/slog"
  slog.Info("message", "key", value, ...)
  slog.Warn("message", "key", value, ...)

For errors/invalid cases use slog.Warn; for success use slog.Info.
Keep all function signatures, error variables, and return behavior unchanged.
All 5 tests must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: import log replaced with import log/slog
log.Printf replaced with slog.Info or slog.Warn calls
Error variables and return values unchanged
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `go test ./...` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
